bc41d83198.q: How does the Protective Insurance Collision Analysis Tool identify crash trends to prevent future collisions?
bc41d83198.a: The Collision Analysis Tool is an Excel-based system with pivot tables that organizes crash data into charts and graphs. It helps identify trends across unlimited time periods, such as which day of the week has the most crashes or seasonal patterns linked to weather. For example, if Tuesday is historically the worst day for crashes, safety directors can schedule safety talks on that day to refocus drivers on safety and prevent incidents.

51019f2c6f.q: What specific data fields does the Protective Collision Analysis Tool capture from FMCSA crash logs?
51019f2c6f.a: The tool captures the required fields mandated by the FMCSA for reportable crashes, plus additional optional fields. It includes data on day of the week, time into shift hours on duty, and weather conditions. The tool is designed so that companies already creating FMCSA crash logs do not have to create two separate logs—they can enter data once and get bonus analysis capabilities, while still being able to print only the FMCSA-required fields if the agency performs an audit.

08929b86ac.q: How do artificial intelligence dash cameras help Protective Insurance clients improve driver safety?
08929b86ac.a: Many Protective clients have adopted AI-powered dash cameras with machine vision that face both forward and toward the driver. The cameras can detect driver inattention through sunglasses and alert the driver with a beep or light while notifying the safety manager by email when events occur. Rather than constant surveillance, the system automatically emails events to safety managers who evaluate the footage and use it as a basis for driver conversations and behavior correction, not as a weapon against drivers.
